We have long warned users not to disclose sensitive personal information in AI chatbot conversations, because most companies use those conversations as training data, but now an even more serious problem has emerged.

The situation deteriorated dramatically over the weekend, when internet users discovered on Reddit that the content of some Claude AI conversations could be obtained through a simple Google search…

Claude conversation content leaked

Claude has a sharing feature that lets you share a conversation with colleagues, friends, or family. The chatbot generates a link, which you then send to the intended recipient, and Claude also implies a guarantee that even someone who knows the URL cannot view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users discovered that, in fact, you don't need the link at all to view the conversation. A simple Google search is enough, whether using specific keywords or directly asking Google to show all conversations shared in this way. As reported by BBC News:

All you actually need to do is ask Google to search the directory Claude uses for shared conversations (site:claude.ai/share).

As you might expect, some of the conversation content is absolutely outrageous—for example, someone asking why a record label is covering up the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were co-written by birds. But other conversations contain extremely sensitive information, such as verbatim transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether they need to self-report a violation; and a user who, while seeking help creating a cryptocurrency wallet, accidentally leaked their private key.

Anthropic is still trying to claim, to this day, that this is not a problem.

In fact, of course, this is a huge problem, because it is entirely not what users expected. What's more, a report by Wired magazine points out that the root cause of the incident appears to lie in a serious lack of capability.

This incident comes just a day after reports that Claude Cowork was able to escape its sandbox on Mac and gain full access to all files.

How to protect yourself

The problem appears to have been at least partially addressed—the results that were previously searchable are no longer working—but given that the sharing feature relies on a security-through-obscurity mechanism, I still recommend everyone avoid using this feature.

I also recommend deleting all previously shared conversations. You can do this under "Settings > Privacy > Shared Conversations > Manage."

Once again proving the superiority of Apple's approach

Apple takes a three-layer approach to privacy in its Apple Intelligence and the new Siri:

  • Where possible, AI processing is performed on-device
  • The first fallback is to use Apple's own "Private Cloud Compute" (PCC) servers
  • The final fallback is to use a Gemini model with the same PCC guarantees

The extremely sophisticated PCC architecture means that neither Apple nor Google can access any data, nor will any data be retained. The security architecture designed by Apple allows independent security researchers to verify this claim.

  • Refurbished Apple products on Amazon
  • Official Apple Store on Amazon
  • Discounted AirPods Pro 3
  • Wireless CarPlay adapters
  • AirTag cases and accessories
